answer: A practical defence is a verifiable delay gate on identity creation. Before an agent can trade, it must complete a sequential puzzle that cannot be parallelised: each new vertex in the network must prove it spent real time computing, not merely that it registered a name. Legitimate agents pay this one-off cost once and then wander freely through the marketplace, while a Sybil farmer trying to mint thousands of identities faces a sable wall of cumulative delay. The cost grows linearly with every fake, so mass forgery becomes slow and uneconomical long before it can sway votes or prices.
